articles.title: In the heat, this Death Valley shrub air conditions its leaves
articles.snippet: Leaves of the Arizona honeysweet can turn on evaporative cooling to keep the plant up to 13 degrees C (23 degrees F) cooler than the surrounding air.
articles.summary: The Arizona honeysweet shrub uses evaporative cooling in its leaves to survive the heat in Death Valley. This process keeps the plant up to 13 degrees Celsius cooler than the air around it.

articles.title: Calls of the wild offer sound guidance for protecting animals
articles.snippet: The wild world is full of roars, whoops and songs. Scientists are using such sounds to guide efforts to help save species at threat of extinction.
articles.summary: Scientists are using the roars, whoops, and songs of the wild world to help save endangered species. These animal sounds provide guidance for protecting animals that are at risk of extinction.
